Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy. The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy. The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

INSPECTION COMMENTS: No violations observed during inspection. Observed gloves to prevent bare hand contact with ready to eat food items such as hot dog buns. Discussed the importance of washing hands in between gloves change, after using restroom, eating, coughing, drinking, and after any possible contamination. Advised staff to use available digital probe thermometer to evaluate the temperatures of potentially hazardous food items during preparation, cooking, cold/hot holding and reheating. Observed all refrigeration unit equipped with monitoring thermometer to ensure unit is adequately cold holding potentially hazardous food items at 45F or less. Reviewed the importance of using time instead of temperature control for potentially hazardous food items listed on facility's waiver by tagging each item immediately after removing from storage or after preparation/cooking. Also discussed, the discard time should be within 4 hours for any potentially hazardous food item after removing from cold holding/ hot holding. No potentially hazardous food items were observed during inspection. Observed test strips to verify the strength of quaternary ammonia sanitizing solution is at least 200 ppm to sanitize food contact surfaces and dishes/utensils. Discussed the significance of wash, rinse and sanitize food contact surfaces/utensils (cutting board, knives) in between food items to prevent cross contamination. Advised manager to work in small, manageable quantities while preparing potentially hazardous food items and return them back to hot or cold holding while not being actively worked on.

Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy. Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and  3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen  information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for,  the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees  on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. DESCRIPTION: Food Service Establishment - Restaurant
INSPECTION COMMENTS: Observed no violations at time of inspection. Observed staff using gloves and tongs when handling ready to eat foods like lemon slices. Observed hand wash sink with warm water, soap, and paper towels. Discussed with staff the importance of washing hands between glove changes, after sneezing, coughing, smoking, handling money, or whenever hands are soiled. Advised staff to replace gloves after tasks such as handling money, prior to returning to food service. Staff produced two analog probe thermometers to ensure potentially hazardous foods (PHFs) are cooked to the required temperature such as chicken wings to 165F. Observed PHFs hot held at or above the required temperature of 140F such as corn and potato soup in the steam table (actual 163F). Observed PHFs cold held at or below the required temperature of 45F such as sliced tomato in the deli prep refrigeration unit (actual 42F). Advised staff to work in small, manageable quantities and place PHFs in hot or cold holding when not actively preparing them. Observed quaternary ammonia sanitizing solution at or above the minimum 200ppm for sanitizing utensils/dishware and food contact surfaces (actual 300ppm). Advised staff to wash, rinse, and sanitize all food contact surfaces to prevent cross contamination. Walk-in cooler floor was replaced at time of inspection. Observed up to date water operation report, with UV bulb at 100%. No visible evidence of pests observed at time of inspection.

Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

At 12:45 pm the inspector observed multiple food items located on the service line steam table that were not at least 140 or higher in hot holding.  Items were temped at approx 110 deg F to 126 deg F.    It is probable that staff were trying to reheat items up in the steam table; it is also possible that the reduced temperature was due to the outage.  At the time of inspection, the inspector was not able to confirm exactly what was going on with the disposition of the food.  Since the food items may have very likely reached 165 deg F in 2 hours (due to smaller batch sizes) no violation is being issued at this time.  Other items such as spanish-style rice, red beans/sauce, and multiple salsas were at acceptable hot holding temperatures.  Five food items were immediately returned to the stove and reheated to at least 165 deg F.   These included ground taco beef/sauce, shredded pork, shredded beef, shredded chicken and black beans.  Operator was directed to reheat all items on stove top to 165 deg F or higher and return to hot holding at 140  deg F.    Inspector educated operator on proper reheat and hot holding temperatures.  Cold holding temperatures in various coolers, the walk in and cooler drawers on the line were all acceptable.

Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

INSPECTION COMMENTS: Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and  3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen  information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for,  the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees  on food allergies. The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and  3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen  information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for,  the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees  on food allergies. Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

INSPECTION COMMENTS: Observed staff wearing gloves to prevent bare hand contact with ready to eat food items such as fresh raw broccoli to stock the salad bar. A digital probe thermometer was available to ensure potentially hazardous food (PHF) items such as raw ground beef is cooked to a minimum required temperature of 158F or above on the flat top grill. Observed PHF items such as tomato slices (actual 39F) and macaroni salad (actual 38F) in the top of the deli prep refrigeration unit as well as raw shrimp (actual 38F) and cooked pasta (actual 41F) in the bottom pull out drawers of the deli refrigeration unit cold holding at the required temperature of 45F or below. Observed PHF items such as fish (actual 41F) in the walk in cooler cold holding at 45F or below. Discussed with the manager cooling method for PHF items such as pasta in pans at a depth of four inches or less placed directly in cooler to ensure that cooling schedule is met at 120-70F in two hours then 70F-45F in additional four hours; for a total of six hours. Advised staff to work in small quantities and to place any food items not actively being prepared back into cold/ hot holding. Advised staff to wash, rinse and sanitize knives and cutting boards to prevent cross contamination. Three hand washing sinks were equipped with warm running water, soap, paper towels and employee hand washing signage. Advised staff of the importance of hand washing between glove changes and after any source of contamination such as eating, drinking, coughing, sneezing, using the rest room and returning to food service after any type of break. Quaternary test strips were available to ensure the strength of the quaternary ammonia sanitizing solution is at a minimum of 200ppm for sanitizing both dishware/ utensils and food contact surfaces. Observed commercial dish washer in final rinse (actual 185F) at required temperature of 180F or above.

The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/fse_signage.htm

Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm.

Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and  3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen  information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for,  the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees  on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/fse_signage.htm
