The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and  3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen  information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for,  the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees  on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and  3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen  information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for,  the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees  on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided. The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness. The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy. In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and  3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen  information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for,  the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees  on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

Upon arrival at 2:00pm the inspector observed a large covered hotel pan full (more than 5 inches deep) of cooked chicken wings at 93F to 96F. The food service worker states the chicken wings were cooked to at least 165F at about 1:30pm and left to cool on the counter for about 15 minutes then placed in the walk in cooler to continue cooking. I advised the cook that the product should ideally be placed in shallow pans, uncovered, in the walk in cooler to rapidly cool from 120F to 70F in 2 hours or less and from 70F to 45F in an additional 4 hours or less. Once cooled the product can be covered and stored in the walk in. A copy of Cooling and Reheating of potentially hazardous foods was provided.

Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm. Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and  3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen  information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for,  the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees  on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

Education regarding the Department’s Food Allergen Law was provided.  The operator was advised that they must post a notice to their employees raising food allergy awareness.  The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies. This notice, and the required menu statement, are available on the Department’s website in English as well as the top six languages spoken in the State; https://www.health.ny.gov/environmental/indoors/food_safety/guidance.htm

The notice must contain information on 1) the process to follow when a customer notifies an employee of a food allergy, 2) how to avoid cross-contact, and 3) the procedures to be followed in the event a customer experiences an allergic reaction, including when to call 9-1-1. The notice must be posted in a conspicuous location, and in at least one of the languages spoken by each employee, provided those languages are among those translated by the Department. The law also requires that food service establishments include the following statement on their menu or menu assembly: “If you have a food allergy, please notify us,” along with a message informing customers that allergen information is available for prepared food items. If the menu is written in a language other than English and is one that the Department makes a translation for, the menu statement must be written in that language. Please be advised that online menus must also include this statement, and a method by which a customer can indicate if they have a food allergy.  In response to this law, the Department created a Food Allergy Awareness notice containing information for food service establishment employees on food allergies.
